headline: Leaders of the White House AI task force were due to meet on Thursday, one of its vice chairs said.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a first working meeting of a new body, with no decisions reported.
importance_line: The meeting shows the task force starting work, which matters to the public and AI companies waiting to see whether it favours voluntary or mandatory rules, but no decisions are reported.
summary: Reuters reports in an exclusive, as relayed by Cryptopolitan, that the leaders of President Trump's AI task force were set to meet on Thursday 8 Oct 2026, according to vice chair Kupor, with a fuller committee session expected next week. This follows our 5 Oct 2026 edition, which carried NBC News's report that Trump created the group and put Jay Clayton in charge; new is a reported 120-day mandate covering cybersecurity, civil liberties, standards for advanced models and overregulation, according to a charter Politico obtained.
notes: Reuters exclusive blocked here (HTTP 401); Economic Times and Investing.com pages gave no text. Text read at Cryptopolitan, which cites Reuters and Politico; its first names for the vice chair are inconsistent, so the entry says only 'vice chair Kupor'. Earlier story: our 5 Oct 2026 edition, item 1 (NBC News).
